2.6 Summary Assuming that holdings of real money balances yield direct utility is a means of ensuring a positive demand for money so that, in equilibrium, money is held and has value. This assumption is clearly a shortcut; it does not address the issue of why money yields utility or why certain pieces of paper that we call money yield utility but other pieces of paper presumably do not. The Sidrauski model, because it assumes that agents act systematically to maximize utility, allows welfare comparisons to be made. The model can be used to assess the welfare costs of inflation and to determine the optimal rate of inflation. Friedman’s conclusion that the optimal inflation rate is the rate that produces a zero nominal rate of interest is quite robust (see chapter 4).
